messages:
lucy: quick sync — ran a 2h profiler sweep on prod last night. saw KV prefix cache hit-rate drop from ~0.92 to ~0.52 during a system-prompt rollout window. list of suspicious signals below.

sahil: do you think this is tokenization drift or just our key scheme being too brittle? :eyes:

lucy: short answer: both. trace samples show many unique keys that are semantically identical to callers but differ only by: JSON field ordering in tool metadata, argument blobs, smart-quote vs ascii-quote, and a subset of hosts running tokenizer v1.2 vs v1.3. tokenizer bump created extra tokens -> longer seq -> different kernel path + no prefix hit.

omar: that sounds nasty. which kernel-paths are flipping?

lucy: mostly the short-seq fast-path -> long-seq fallback. kernel selector trips when input length crosses ~128 tokens; added 6–12 tokens from tokenizer diffs pushed many requests over. once on fallback path, latency + mem patterns change so prefix cache entries aren't compatible.

maja: can we canonicalize the key to avoid harmless differences? e.g. normalize quotes, collapse whitespace, stable-sort JSON fields?

sahil: proposal: keep tokenizer_version pinned in key (so we don't mix incompatible tokenizations) but canonicalize visible prompt text and drop variable tool args. include function/tool identity but not argument values.

lucy: exactly. proposed key bits: model_id | tokenizer_pin | normalized_prompt | tool_schema_hash. normalized_prompt does: trim, collapse repeated whitespace, normalize unicode quotes -> ascii, and canonicalize JSON-ish tool descriptors when present. we should avoid including raw argument blobs.

omar: agree on excluding args. arguments are often unique and will kill reuse. what about request-level metadata like request_id or timestamps? drop them for sure.

lucy: experiment plan:
A) canary deploy a canonicalizer that strips args + sorts tool/metadata fields (10% traffic)
B) pin tokenizer version in the key for canary hosts (v1.3) to avoid cross-version collisions
C) add new metric: kernel-path-churn correlated with cache-miss spikes and prefix eviction rates

deploy-bot: deployment queued: canary-canonicalizer -> eng-runtime-canary (10%).

sahil: one more optimization idea: instead of hashing entire system prompt text, include an 8-byte rolling delta checksum (fast) plus normalized prefix hash. gives us cheap change-detection but tolerant to trivial whitespace diffs.

lucy: good call. will implement a delta-hash (Blake2b-64) for system prompt component. still include normalized_prompt hash for absolute correctness in offline checks.

maja: side note on eviction: current LRU per-prefix is getting thrashed when long-system-prompt workloads (image-gen pipelines) flood with unique leading tokens. propose bucketized caps: group prefixes by normalized leading-8-tokens and cap entries per bucket to keep hot prefixes sticky.

omar: timeline? can we get a latency regression guard?

lucy: canary today. checks:
- hit-rate goal: +5–10% recovery in canary vs baseline
- no >3% p95 latency regression on canary
- kernel-path churn down vs baseline
if green, rollout tomorrow. I'll post dashboards.

maja: I'll own instrumentation for kernel-path metric and add traces for top N misses so we can see exact token diffs.

sahil: small follow-up test: add a unit test where tokenizer v1.3 tokenizes `“smart” quotes` differently; canonicalizer should normalize to `"` and produce same key as v1.2.

lucy: adding unit + integration tests. example canonical key generation (pseudocode):
```
key_input = model + '|' + tokenizer_pin + '|' + normalize(prompt_text) + '|' + tool_schema_fingerprint
cache_key = sha256(key_input)
```

sahil: :thumbsup: thanks. let's also log a small sample of dropped-args hashes (not contents) so we can debug correctness without storing full PII/args.

lucy: will do. will post canary results here once available.
